name: Corner Cubes Characterize Initial Opposite-Section Locking
statement: Let $A$ be ample with marked concept $a$, and in every active coordinate call the section containing $a$ lower. Every corner of every opposite section lies in its overlap with the lower section if and only if $a$ belongs to the unique maximal cube of every corner $c$ of $A$. Equivalently, the coordinates on which $c$ differs from $a$ are all incident directions of $c$.
proof: A corner of an opposite section outside the overlap has no mate across the split coordinate. Its lift is therefore a corner of $A$ with the same incident support, and the split coordinate separates it from $a$ without belonging to that support. Conversely, any such separating nonincident coordinate places the entire corner cube in the opposite section and leaves its projection as a corner outside the overlap. Excluding all such coordinates is exactly the condition that $a$ lies in every corner cube.
